1. Executive Summary & Scope

This verification report validates the input domains, edge conditions, and automated decision logic of the AI Disaster Response & Resource Allocation System using Equivalence Class Partitioning (ECP). By subdividing input domains into disjoint subsets of valid (VEC) and invalid (IEC) values, representative test cases were selected to prove that valid emergency workflows succeed and boundary violations are trapped deterministically.

Verification Conclusion: All 17 Equivalence Partitions evaluated across Registration, Authentication, Incident Intake & AI Triage, and Transactional Resource Allocation passed without regressions.

2. Equivalence Class Partitioning Methodology

Given an input domain D, equivalence partitioning derives disjoint subsets P1, P2, ... Pn such that any test vector within Pi yields an equivalent system response. In this audit, parameters were partitioned into:

  • Valid Equivalence Classes (VEC): Inputs satisfying operational bounds (Name 2-100 chars, RFC Email, Password >= 8 chars, GPS bounds, Quantity 1 to Available Stock).
  • Invalid Equivalence Classes (IEC): Inputs violating system bounds (< 2 characters, non-RFC email, mismatched passwords, missing coordinates, Quantity <= 0, over-allocation Quantity > Stock).

5. Key Engineering Observations

  • AI Triage Substring Heuristic: The AI triage engine inspects keywords using substring inclusion (text.includes("trapped")). When testing low-severity reports, the phrase "no trapped victims" inadvertently triggered critical escalation to Severity 7/10. It is recommended to add negation phrase detection in aiTriageService.js.
  • Dual-Layer Input Validation: Browser HTML5 constraint validation intercepts submission natively before React JavaScript validation handlers fire. Automated tests must check native checkValidity() and test state errors using form.noValidate = true.
  • Transactional Stock Protection: Over-allocation and zero/negative quantities are blocked client-side by disabling the submission trigger and displaying reactive remaining-stock calculations.
